title: PH-04 Chile Peppers in Space
takeaway: Chile pepper plants grew in a plant chamber on the International Space Station for 137 days, one of the longest plant-growing tests there, and made 26 peppers.

title: Microbiological and nutritional analysis of lettuce crops grown on the International Space Station-VEG01A
takeaway: Scientists grew red romaine lettuce in the Veggie plant chamber on the space station and compared it with lettuce grown on Earth to check that space-grown food is safe and healthy to eat.

title: Adaptive response of Arabidopsis seedlings in microgravity and Mars reduced gravity environment is enhanced by red light photostimulation
takeaway: Scientists grew tiny seedlings on the space station in weightlessness and in Mars-strength gravity, and found that the Mars-gravity seedlings only got their growing cells back on track when they were given red light.

title: A molecular study of Italian ryegrass grown on Martian regolith simulant
takeaway: Scientists on Earth grew ryegrass in pretend Mars soil: the plants grew for two weeks, but their leaves turned yellowish and bent downward.

title: Approaches for Surveying Cosmic Radiation Damage in Large Populations of Arabidopsis thaliana Seeds- an Antarctic Example
takeaway: Scientists sent about 580,000 tiny plant seeds high above Antarctica on a balloon to study cosmic radiation, and those seeds sprouted less often and had more mutations than seeds that stayed safe in the lab.

title: Microgravity and space radiation exert either opposite or synergic effects on single molecular pathways
takeaway: Scientists flew human blood-vessel cells to the space station and found that space radiation and weightlessness change the cells in different ways, with radiation switching on the cells’ DNA-repair systems.

title: The impact of deep space radiation on cognitive performance: From biological sex to biomarkers to countermeasures (Elevated Plus Maze, Novel Object Recognition, Open Field, Radial Arm Water Maze, and Three Chamber Social Isolation/Interaction)
takeaway: Scientists on Earth used a particle accelerator to give mice radiation like the kind found in deep space; afterward the male mice had more trouble learning their way through a maze, but the female mice did not.

title: Lunar gravity prevents skeletal muscle atrophy but not myofiber type shift in mice
takeaway: On the space station, mice that rode in a spinning habitat with Moon-strength gravity kept their leg muscle size, while mice in weightlessness lost some.

title: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight [plasma proteomics]
takeaway: Mice that spent 33 days on the space station lost muscle and bone, so scientists tested a treatment that helped mice build muscle and bone, both in space and on the ground.

title: Osteocytes transcriptome is altered during spaceflight
takeaway: Scientists flew bone cells to the space station for 2 to 6 days to learn how bones sense weightlessness, because astronauts lose bone on long trips.
